n6e0131fbfa9.s: Under the Cabinet Mission scheme, the representatives of the princely states in the Constituent Assembly were to be:
o: Directly elected by the people of the states
Nominated by the rulers of the states
n6e0131fbfa9.x: Princely-state members were to be nominated by the rulers, not directly elected; provincial members were elected community-wise by PR-STV.

n8badbe2b009.s: The Wavell Plan proposed equal representation in the Executive Council for:
n8badbe2b009.x: The Wavell Plan proposed parity between caste Hindus and Muslims, with the Viceroy and Commander-in-Chief excluded from Indianisation.

nae58d5b4045.s: According to the Cabinet Mission, non-Muslims formed about what share of the population of the proposed north-eastern zone of Pakistan?
nae58d5b4045.x: The Mission noted non-Muslim populations of 38% in the north-west and 48% in the north-east, one reason it rejected a full Pakistan.

n247dd15c9aa.s: The Simla Conference, whose failure gave the Muslim League a de facto veto over constitutional progress, closed abruptly on:
n247dd15c9aa.x: The Simla Conference closed abruptly on 14 July 1945, handing the Muslim League a de facto veto.

nindian-history-117-18.s: The Shimla Conference (1945) is associated with:
nindian-history-117-18.x: The Wavell Plan led to the Shimla Conference; Cripps offered Dominion Status and the Cabinet Mission planned the Constituent Assembly.

nd70636bbbbc.s: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, how many seats in the Constituent Assembly were allotted to British India?
nd70636bbbbc.x: British India got 296 seats and the princely states 93, roughly one seat per ten lakh population.

nffce1dc8bd6.s: The Gandhi-Jinnah talks of September 1944 were held on the basis of:
nffce1dc8bd6.x: The Gandhi-Jinnah talks (Bombay, 9-27 Sept 1944) were based on the C.R. Formula, which proposed a post-war plebiscite in contiguous Muslim-majority areas.

n456444ea0f9.s: In the 1945-46 elections, how many of the 30 Muslim seats in the Central Legislative Assembly did the Muslim League win?
n456444ea0f9.x: The League won all 30 Muslim seats in the Central Legislative Assembly, while the Congress swept the general seats.

n5dd17cc2e6d.s: Under the three-tier structure of the Cabinet Mission Plan, residuary subjects were vested in:
n5dd17cc2e6d.x: The plan proposed a Union, groups of provinces and provinces, with the provinces holding all residuary subjects.

nc7dc5198e77.s: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, Group B of provinces consisted of:
nc7dc5198e77.x: Group B was Punjab, NWFP and Sindh (Muslim-majority north-west); Group C was Bengal and Assam, and Group A included Madras, Bombay, UP, Bihar, CP and Orissa.

n922b5af675d.s: In which year did the Congress adopt the demand for a Constituent Assembly?
n922b5af675d.x: M.N. Roy raised the demand in 1934, the Congress adopted it in 1935, and the August Offer accepted it in 1940.

nindian-history-105-15.s: The first Interim Government headed by Nehru took office on:
nindian-history-105-15.x: Wavell invited Nehru on 12 August 1946 and the Interim Government took office on 2 September 1946.

n96bec2b1eda.s: The Simla Conference of June-July 1945 was convened to discuss the:
n96bec2b1eda.x: The Simla Conference (June-July 1945) discussed the Wavell Plan of 1945.

n349edabedeb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Mountbatten Plan?
o: The Punjab and Bengal assemblies were to vote on partition in two parts.
Sindh was to decide on partition through its own legislative assembly.
Princely states were given a third option of remaining completely independent.
Referendums were provided for in NWFP and Sylhet district.
n349edabedeb.x: No third option was provided: paramountcy lapsed and the states could join India or Pakistan.

nbe161dd4d38.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
A. Mountbatten Plan
B. Attlee Statement on transfer of power
C. Lord Mountbatten replaces Lord Wavell as Viceroy
D. Independence of India
nbe161dd4d38.x: The Attlee Statement (20 February 1947) was followed by Mountbatten replacing Wavell, then the Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947) and independence (15 August 1947).

nc891b6efdec.x: India Divided was written by Rajendra Prasad; Azad wrote India Wins Freedom and Khushwant Singh Train to Pakistan.

n4fa6aa8b8f1.s: Under the Indian Independence Act, 1947, the Constituent Assemblies of the two dominions were given ____ power to frame any Constitution.
n4fa6aa8b8f1.x: The Act gave the Constituent Assemblies sovereign power, including the power to repeal any British law, even the Independence Act itself.

n7c342b7914a.s: The Radcliffe Line award was announced on:
n7c342b7914a.x: The Radcliffe award was announced on 17 August 1947, after independence.

na0cf3dd32a1.s: Plan Balkan, an earlier scheme of Lord Mountbatten (May 1947), was rejected by:
na0cf3dd32a1.x: Nehru rejected Plan Balkan because it could lead to the Balkanisation of India.

n9ad15beeae8.s: At Partition, what share of the assets and liabilities went to Pakistan?
n9ad15beeae8.x: The Partition Council gave Pakistan 17.5 per cent of the assets and liabilities, not 25 per cent.

n4811282710d.s: In March 1947, Gandhi went to ____ to calm riots against Muslims.
n4811282710d.x: After his Noakhali mission (Nov 1946 - Mar 1947), Gandhi went to Bihar in March 1947 to calm anti-Muslim riots.

n55845851cc8.s: Which of the following offices was ended by the Indian Independence Act, 1947?
o: Chief Justice of the Federal Court
n55845851cc8.x: The Act ended the offices of the Viceroy and the Secretary of State, lapsed paramountcy and provided for boundary commissions.

nindian-history-22-16.s: The Communal Award was announced by:
nindian-history-22-16.x: British PM Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award; the Poona Pact followed it.

n0f507702136.s: The Bole Resolution (1923), which opened public watering places to untouchables, was passed by the:
n0f507702136.x: The Bole Resolution of 1923 was passed by the Bombay Legislative Council; Mahad Municipality's 1924 decision stayed on paper.

n1d4dd0a3c2d.s: The Poona Pact is often referred to as the:
n1d4dd0a3c2d.x: The Poona Pact is often called the Gandhi-Ambedkar Pact; it replaced separate electorates with joint electorates.

nindian-history-98-15.s: Apart from Gandhi, the Poona Pact is associated with:
nindian-history-98-15.x: The Poona Pact involved B.R. Ambedkar; Irwin, Jinnah and Liaquat Ali Khan are linked to other pacts and talks.

nindian-history-98-9.s: The Lucknow Pact was concluded in:
nindian-history-98-9.x: The Lucknow Pact was 1916; 1931 is the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, 1932 the Poona Pact and 1944 the Gandhi-Jinnah talks.

nindian-history-99-4.s: The Second Round Table Conference was held during:
nindian-history-99-4.x: The Second RTC ran 7 September - 1 December 1931; the First was Nov 1930 - Jan 1931 and the Third 17 Nov - 24 Dec 1932.

n62350dee57b.s: Mahatma Gandhi attended which Round Table Conference(s)?
n62350dee57b.x: Gandhi attended only the Second RTC (1931), while Ambedkar attended all three.

nindian-history-99-8.s: Which party stayed away from the First Round Table Conference?
nindian-history-99-8.x: The Congress was absent from the First RTC, where Ambedkar demanded separate electorates for the Depressed Classes.

nindian-history-98-7.s: The Poona Pact was concluded in:
nindian-history-98-7.x: The Poona Pact of September 1932 dealt with Depressed Classes representation through reserved seats in joint electorates.

nindian-history-100-11.x: Gandhi started Harijan in 1933, a year after founding the All India Anti-Untouchability League (1932).

nindian-history-99-6.s: At the Second Round Table Conference, Ambedkar demanded ____ for the Depressed Classes.
nindian-history-99-6.x: Ambedkar's demand for separate electorates, with other minority claims, caused the communal deadlock that wrecked the Second RTC.

nindian-history-100-33.s: Which of the following signed the Poona Pact (1932)?
nindian-history-100-33.x: The Pact was signed by representatives such as Madan Mohan Malaviya and Ambedkar; Gandhi did not sign it himself.

nindian-history-98-11.s: The Lucknow Pact (1916) between the Congress and the Muslim League accepted ____ for Muslims.
nindian-history-98-11.x: The Lucknow Pact accepted separate electorates for Muslims rather than rejecting them.

nf329f137a15.s: Which of the following was written by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar?
nf329f137a15.x: The Problem of the Rupee is Ambedkar's work; Servants of India is not his.

nf418fcec867.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched regarding Ambedkar's view of Indian federalism?
o: States – right to secede from the Union
Centre – strong, to protect weaker sections
System – unitary or federal as times require
nf418fcec867.x: Ambedkar held the Union indestructible, so States have no right to secede; the other pairs reflect his views.

na78a9f895b9.s: The Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly was set up on:
na78a9f895b9.x: It was set up on 29 August 1947 with seven members, including chairman Ambedkar; Nehru was not a member.

nf75c25aa6e1.s: During the debates on its making, the Indian Constitution was criticised as a copy of the:
nf75c25aa6e1.x: Critics called it a 'copy of the Government of India Act, 1935' and a 'lawyers' paradise'.

nf463b71d0df.s: Ambedkar borrowed the term 'constitutional morality' from:
nf463b71d0df.x: Ambedkar took the term from George Grote and said constitutional morality has to be cultivated.

n7408f72f81e.s: Who was originally the only Congress member of the Drafting Committee?
n7408f72f81e.x: K.M. Munshi, who also chaired the Order of Business Committee, was originally the only Congress member of the Drafting Committee.

n8e504de9000.s: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?
n8e504de9000.x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and makes it punishable; Articles 15-16 cover non-discrimination and Article 46 the welfare of SCs/STs.

n7a58617c70b.s: Which of the following pairs regarding Ambedkar's conversion to Buddhism is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Followers who accompanied him – about fifty thousand
n7a58617c70b.x: About five lakh followers, mostly Mahars, accompanied him, not fifty thousand; the other pairs are correct.

na9b21027bfb.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar suggested which city as a second capital of India?
na9b21027bfb.x: Ambedkar suggested Hyderabad as a second capital; he also proposed dividing Maharashtra and warned against huge states.

n000bcfd5a1a.s: Who supported Ambedkar's idea of considering Sikhism as an alternative to Hinduism?
n000bcfd5a1a.x: B.S. Moonje supported the idea, while Gandhi, Rajagopalachari and Malaviya opposed it.

nd6c88bd2535.s: The term 'Harijan' for the depressed classes was used by:
nd6c88bd2535.x: Gandhi used the term 'Harijan'; Ambedkar rejected it in favour of Dalit/Scheduled Castes.

n37637db5504.s: Gandhi and Ambedkar differed fundamentally on:
o: Whether the whole caste system should be annihilated
n37637db5504.x: Both sought uplift of the marginalised and stressed education, but differed on whether the whole caste system should be annihilated.

n46d7368aa3a.s: Ambedkar called the Indian village 'a sink of localism, a den of ignorance, narrow-mindedness and communalism' in the Constituent Assembly on:
n46d7368aa3a.x: He said this on 4 November 1948, preferring the individual, not the village, as the basic unit.

nbd2d09906f5.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar founded the Independent Labour Party in:
nbd2d09906f5.x: He founded the ILP in 1936 and was Labour Member during 1942-46.

nc33b21ac837.s: Ambedkar set out his proposals for State socialism in:
nc33b21ac837.x: States and Minorities proposed State ownership of key industries and agricultural land and nationalised insurance.

n23591003016.s: "Nothing can emancipate the outcaste except the destruction of the caste system." Who said this?
n23591003016.x: The statement is B.R. Ambedkar's (APPSC-G1 2018), in line with Annihilation of Caste (1936).

n077691a21af.s: Under the Cabinet Mission scheme, provincial members of the Constituent Assembly were elected by:
o: Proportional representation by single transferable vote
n077691a21af.x: Each community's members in the provincial assembly elected its representatives by PR-STV, with seats divided broadly by population.

n4054668d2e1.s: Which member of the Constituent Assembly founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha?
n4054668d2e1.x: Durgabai Deshmukh founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha; Pattabhi Sitaramayya chaired the House Committee and Ranga was a peasant leader.

nb1b5675cba4.s: Pingali Venkayya showed his 1921 tricolour design to Gandhi at the AICC session held at:
nb1b5675cba4.x: Venkayya presented the design at the Bezwada AICC session; Gandhi added the charkha, later replaced by the Ashoka Chakra.

n47c1c1dd871.s: Who first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India in 1934?
n47c1c1dd871.x: M.N. Roy proposed it in 1934; the INC made it an official demand in 1935 and the August Offer accepted it in 1940.

n0d982609b81.s: Jawaharlal Nehru accepted the Andhra demand in the Constituent Assembly on:
n0d982609b81.x: Nehru accepted it on 27 November 1947; Andhra was dropped from the Draft Constitution on 21 February 1948 and the Dhar Commission named on 17 June 1948.

n5d8a85cdcf7.s: The National Development Council was set up on:
n5d8a85cdcf7.x: The NDC was set up on 6 August 1952, chaired by the PM, and gave final approval to Five Year Plans.

n6e540923401.s: Indian secularism differs from the Western model of strict separation mainly because the Indian State:
o: May intervene to reform certain social practices
n6e540923401.x: India has no State religion and stays neutral, but unlike the Western model it permits State intervention for social reform.

n26e74222cba.s: The Planning Commission was set up on 15 March 1950 by:
n26e74222cba.x: It was set up by an executive resolution and was replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015.

nb20ef5a7463.s: The Bandung Conference of 1955 was sponsored by:
nb20ef5a7463.x: The Colombo Powers (India, Indonesia, Burma, Ceylon, Pakistan) sponsored Bandung, where Panchsheel was absorbed into the Ten Principles.

na7c3564fdf7.s: China's construction of a road through ____ was one of the causes of the India-China war of 1962.
na7c3564fdf7.x: China's road through Aksai Chin, with the McMahon Line dispute, the Dalai Lama's asylum and the Forward Policy, led to the 1962 war.

n10776ad4c25.s: The Third Five Year Plan (1961-66) was called the:
n10776ad4c25.x: The Third Plan was the 'Gadgil Yojana', based on the Sandy-Chakravarty model; it was derailed by the 1962 and 1965 wars and drought.

n518034b3366.s: China declared a unilateral ceasefire in the 1962 war on:
n518034b3366.x: China declared a unilateral ceasefire on 21 November 1962; India's National Emergency was declared on 26 October 1962.

nf93823be514.s: The Mahalanobis strategy gave primary emphasis to:
nf93823be514.x: The Mahalanobis strategy stressed industrial development and was criticised for neglecting agriculture.

n6bcce775818.s: The UGC, set up in 1953, became a statutory body under the UGC Act of:
n6bcce775818.x: The UGC became statutory under the UGC Act, 1956; it is not a constitutional body.

ne113fc21968.s: Which was the first country outside India and China to adopt Panchsheel (1954)?
ne113fc21968.x: Burma was the first country outside the India-China pair to adopt Panchsheel in 1954, not Indonesia.

n7fcf131679e.s: Goa was liberated through Operation Vijay in:
n7fcf131679e.x: Goa was liberated in December 1961, after the Dalai Lama's flight (1959) and Chou En-lai's visit (1960).

n514ead6cb25.s: In which year was the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act enacted?
n514ead6cb25.x: It was enacted in 1956, the same year as the Hindu Succession and Minority and Guardianship Acts; the Hindu Marriage Act was 1955.

nf99b2c14ddc.s: Which of the following was an influence on Jawaharlal Nehru?
nf99b2c14ddc.x: Nehru was influenced by Fabian socialism, British liberalism, Gandhi and Soviet planning; German nationalism was not an influence.

nbd89c7ec931.s: Panchsheel's principles include mutual respect for sovereignty, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, peaceful co-existence and ____.
o: Collective military defence against power blocs
nbd89c7ec931.x: Non-aggression is one of the five Panchsheel principles; collective military defence against power blocs was not.

n2fdb058afa1.s:
Assertion (A): Potti Sriramulu's constructive work included khadi, prohibition and Harijan uplift.
Reason (R): Potti Sriramulu was born in Nellore town, his ancestral village.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n2fdb058afa1.x: A is true. R is false: he was born in Madras, and his ancestral village was Gajula Dinne in Nellore district.

n130e78c805e.s: The first Vice-Chancellor of Andhra University was:
n130e78c805e.x: C.R. Reddy was the first VC of Andhra University, set up under the 1925 Act passed by the Justice Party government.

nb9049f1860c.s: The demand for a separate Andhra university was first raised at the first session of the Andhra Mahasabha in:
nb9049f1860c.x: The university demand was first raised at the first session in 1913; Telugu as medium of instruction was demanded at the third session in 1915.

n10c8bc94a4f.s: Ramadasu Pantulu moved an Andhra state proposal in the Council of State in:
n10c8bc94a4f.x: Ramadasu Pantulu moved the Andhra state proposal in 1926; in 1925 he had amended Dr. Ramarao's resolution to seek linguistic states.

n4088de8c2e0.s: The agenda of the Bapatla session of 1913 included lifting the ban on the entry of Telugus into the:
n4088de8c2e0.x: The Bapatla agenda included removal of the ban on Telugus entering the Army, an English paper and a fund for technical training abroad.

nf78883f8c8e.s: Who moved the early proposal for a separate Andhra province, which Nyapati Subba Rao opposed?
nf78883f8c8e.x: The proposal was moved by Vemavarapu Ramadasu Pantulu; Krishna Rao moved the amendment and a committee under Pattabhi Sitaramayya followed.

n73a24f07f55.s: During his 1948 visit to ____, Nehru promised a committee on the Andhra/linguistic province issue.
n73a24f07f55.x: Nehru promised a committee during his 1948 Visakhapatnam visit, part of the background to the Dar Commission and JVP Committee.

n1f04ee553e1.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement provided for an Andhra–Telangana cabinet ratio of:
n1f04ee553e1.x: It provided a 60:40 cabinet ratio, a Telangana Regional Committee, protection of surplus funds and job/education safeguards.

n426d6e4637b.s: In the Madras Presidency, how many Deputy Collector posts were held by Telugus?
n426d6e4637b.x: Telugus held 21 Deputy Collector posts, 30 District Munsif posts and no District Judge posts; they held 8 high State jobs against 56 for non-Telugus.

n6423ba4143b.s: Who presided over the fourth Andhra Mahasabha at Kakinada (1916) and was called the 'Gokhale of South India'?
n6423ba4143b.x: Mocherla Ramachandra Rao, the 'Gokhale of South India', presided at Kakinada; a women's session was held there under Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi.

n7a85a5893d9.s: The 1955 mid-term election in Andhra State followed the fall of the ministry headed by:
n7a85a5893d9.x: It followed the fall of Prakasam's ministry; the United Congress front (Congress, Krishikar Lok Party, PSP) contested against the Communists.

n10e56a9febf.s: The JVP Committee's report reaffirmed the general approach of the:
n10e56a9febf.x: The JVP report reaffirmed the Dhar approach, putting security, unity and economic prosperity above immediate linguistic reorganisation.

nda428f3f48b.s: Which leader, and later Kamaraj, opposed sharing Madras city with the Andhras?
nda428f3f48b.x: Rajaji and later Kamaraj opposed sharing Madras; the JVP formula required the Andhras to drop their claim to it.

nf9037a36302.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the session of the Indian National Congress held in 1948 at:
nf9037a36302.x: He presided at Jaipur in 1948; at Tripuri (1939) he had lost to Subhas Bose despite Gandhi's backing.

n086f50cc5ec.s: Who presided over the Silver Jubilee session of the Andhra Mahasabha at Vijayawada in 1937?
n086f50cc5ec.x: Kadapa Koti Reddy presided over the 1937 session (and the 1931 Special Andhra Sabha); H.M. Sitaram Reddy only inaugurated it.

n11d7700a3bd.s: After the Bapatla conference of 1913, which district meeting considered the separate Andhra demand 'not yet ripe'?
n11d7700a3bd.x: Nellore called the demand 'not yet ripe', while Guntur, Vijayawada, Godavari, Vizag and Chittoor backed it.

n9ba5bcfd0b5.s: Sir Vijayanand ('Sir Vijaya') presided over the Andhra Mahasabha session held in November 1941 at:
n9ba5bcfd0b5.x: He presided at Visakhapatnam in November 1941 and met Stafford Cripps on 2 April 1942.

n4a933e2296b.s: The 58-foot 'Statue of Sacrifice' of Potti Sriramulu at Amaravati was unveiled on 16 March 2026, his:
n4a933e2296b.x: Born 16 March 1901, Sriramulu's 125th birth anniversary fell on 16 March 2026, when CM Chandrababu Naidu unveiled the statue.

nc0766e993be.s: Apart from Jawaharlal Nehru and Vallabhbhai Patel, the third member of the JVP Committee was:
nc0766e993be.x: The three members were Nehru, Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya; N. Sanjiva Reddy was not a member.

n447ce84f2c4.s: In the April 1951 APCC election, Sanjiva Reddy defeated N.G. Ranga by a margin of:
n447ce84f2c4.x: Sanjiva Reddy won by five votes, after which Prakasam and Ranga formed the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party.

ne6afe9d1121.s: Andhra University was inaugurated at Waltair on:
ne6afe9d1121.x: After Subbaroyan's ministry fixed the seat at Visakhapatnam (December 1928), it was inaugurated at Waltair on 5 September 1930.

n02d042eb27d.s: Deshabhimani, the Anglo-Telugu paper that on 4 February 1910 called for a political meeting on Andhra problems, was published from:
n02d042eb27d.x: Deshabhimani was published from Guntur, with editorials by Seshagirirao.

n70c9a362a10.s: The High Court of Andhra State at Guntur was set up on:
n70c9a362a10.x: It was set up on 5 July 1954; until then the Madras High Court served Andhra State.

n0bb57b5a90d.s: At the 1937 Silver Jubilee session, Rayalaseema leaders demanded safeguards relating to:
o: Separate army recruitment and the capital
Cabinet representation and separate army recruitment
Cabinet representation, irrigation and the capital
n0bb57b5a90d.x: The 1937 safeguards concerned Cabinet representation, irrigation and the capital; separate army recruitment was not among them.

n502b290b7e2.s: The Andhra Provincial Congress Committee was formed in:
n502b290b7e2.x: The Andhra PCC was formed in 1918 and became a regular linguistic unit after the Nagpur session.

n17b0145f38f.s: Andhra was dropped from the Draft Constitution published on:
n17b0145f38f.x: Andhra, first in the Draft's First Schedule, was omitted from the Draft of 21 February 1948 after Tamil and Kannada objections.

n4e546ab4758.s: In the Madras Assembly vote on the capital of Andhra State, Kurnool defeated Vijayawada by:
n4e546ab4758.x: Kurnool won 79 to 53, helped by five non-Andhra votes; Prakasam did not vote.

n1ffe04f8030.s: The Sreebagh Pact was concluded on:
n1ffe04f8030.x: The Sreebagh Pact of 16 November 1937 put the capital and High Court in different regions and gave Rayalaseema first choice.

n8b2a3779c2b.s: Who among the following supported B.N. Sarma's 1918 resolution?
n8b2a3779c2b.x: K.V. Rangaswami Ayyangar supported it, while Jinnah and V.S. Srinivasa Sastri opposed it.

ncca1b9ba599.s: Manda Suryanarayana, who presided over the Vizag district meeting of June 1913, was the municipal chairman of:
ncca1b9ba599.x: Manda Suryanarayana was Vizianagaram's municipal chairman; Guntur's first was Vinjamuri Bhavanacharyulu. The meeting started the weekly Andhra Advocate.

n827994299bd.s: The first Rayalaseema Mahasabha (28 January 1934) demanded a separate university at:
n827994299bd.x: Presided over by Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao, it opposed inclusion in Andhra University and demanded a separate university at Tirupati.

n3d68117d01c.s: Who was the secretary of the first Andhra Mahasabha at Bapatla (1913)?
n3d68117d01c.x: Konda Venkatappayya was secretary (APPSC 2022 key) of the Bapatla Mahasabha of 26 May 1913.

n478060b7380.s: Who presided over the first Andhra Mahasabha at Bapatla on 26 May 1913?
n478060b7380.x: B.N. Sarma presided at Bapatla; the province resolution was deferred, not passed, there.

nf390dcb5a1e.s: The Wanchoo inquiry was conducted during:
nf390dcb5a1e.x: The Wanchoo inquiry was held in February–March 1953, after the Dhar Commission, JVP Committee and the Madras Partition Committee (1949–50).

nf8d8d4f66d1.s: The JVP Committee was constituted in December 1948 at the AICC session held at:
nf8d8d4f66d1.x: It was constituted at the Jaipur AICC session (December 1948) with Pattabhi Sitaramayya as president and reported in 1949.

n96491ee1ced.s: Andhra Patrika was originally founded in:
n96491ee1ced.x: Andhra Patrika was founded in Bombay, moved to Madras and became a daily in 1914.

n9770692d449.s: The Dar Commission (June 1948) was appointed by the:
n9770692d449.x: It was appointed by the President of the Constituent Assembly in June 1948, with S.K. Dhar as chairman.

nac2b658fff3.s: Swami Sitaram's fast for a separate Andhra State in 1951 lasted:
nac2b658fff3.x: Swami Sitaram fasted for 35 days in 1951 for a separate Andhra State.

nce17deda7ea.s: Who founded Andhra Kesari at Rajahmundry in 1904 and wrote Andhrula Charitra?
nce17deda7ea.x: Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao did both; Andhra Patrika is associated with Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.

n7154157fb5b.s: At its formation in 1953, Andhra State had how many districts?
n7154157fb5b.x: Andhra State had 11 districts: 7 in Coastal Andhra and 4 in Rayalaseema.

nc6fa40fcbe3.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was 'Andhra Ratna'; 'Deshabhakta' was Konda Venkatappayya.

n44e447c13b3.s: In the Madras city question, who proposed the Cooum river as the boundary?
n44e447c13b3.x: Panaganti Ramarayaningar proposed the Cooum boundary in the early 1920s; Kadapa Koti Reddy proposed Madras as capital in 1933.

nap-history-33-5.s: N.T. Rama Rao founded the Telugu Desam Party on:
nap-history-33-5.x: NTR founded the TDP on 29 March 1982, not 29 May.

nap-history-17-5.s: The second session of the Vishalandhra Mahasabha, held at Hyderabad in 1954, was presided over by:
nap-history-17-5.x: K.V. Ranga Reddy presided over the 1954 session; Swamy Ramananda Tirtha strongly supported Vishalandhra.

n459855763c6.s: In which year did the Madras session block the Andhra resolution?
n459855763c6.x: Madras blocked it in 1914, the provincial conference refused it in 1915, Lucknow took no decision in 1916 and a committee followed in 1918.

nap-history-1-28.s: Who was the first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha in Andhra?
nap-history-1-28.x: Vallabhaneni Sitamahalakshmi was the first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha in Andhra.

nf41eb010143.s: Potti Sriramulu died during his fast for Andhra State on:
nf41eb010143.x: He began fasting on 19 October 1952 and died on 15 December 1952; Nehru announced Andhra State on 19 December 1952.

nap-history-17-9.s: The 1936 Andhra Mahasabha convention, which sought to bridge the trust deficit between Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema leaders, was held at:
nap-history-17-9.x: The 1936 convention met at Bellary and paved the way for the Sribagh Pact of 1937.

nap-history-1-6.s: Who was the first President of the Hyderabad State Congress?
nap-history-1-6.x: Govinda Rao Nanal was the first President of the Hyderabad State Congress.

n955895352f7.s: Who became Chief Minister of Andhra State after the 1955 mid-term election?
n955895352f7.x: Prakasam (CM from 1 October 1953) fell in November 1954; after the 1955 poll Bezawada Gopala Reddy became CM.

nap-history-1-11.s: The Andhra Pradesh Legislature became bicameral for the first time in:
nap-history-1-11.x: The Legislative Council was created in 1958, making the legislature bicameral.

nap-history-17-14.s: The Andhra Jana Sangham, formed in Hyderabad in 1921 and later renamed the Andhra Mahasabha, was led by:
nap-history-17-14.x: Madapati Hanumantha Rao led the Andhra Jana Sangham, later restructured as the Andhra Mahasabha.

nap-history-33-18.s: Gandhi visited Hyderabad on 9 March of which year?
nap-history-33-18.x: Gandhi's Hyderabad visit was on 9 March 1934, the same year as the first Rayalaseema Mahasabha (28 January).

nap-history-19-5.s: Who was the first Chief Justice of the High Court of Andhra State at Guntur?
nap-history-19-5.x: Koka Subba Rao was the first Chief Justice of the Andhra High Court, set up at Guntur in 1954.

n6010076e035.s: Along with a separate university, the early Andhra movement demanded a port at:
n6010076e035.x: The university demand came with demands for agricultural and medical colleges and a port at Visakhapatnam.

n0ccf0c8db4f.s: The Andhra State Bill received assent on:
n0ccf0c8db4f.x: Introduced on 10 August 1953, the Bill received assent on 14 September 1953, and Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953.

n04962f32204.s: Konda Venkatappayya came to prominence among the Andhra Moderates after:
n04962f32204.x: Konda Venkatappayya rose among Andhra Moderates after 1908, so he was not an Andhra delegate at the first INC session of 1885.

naa8b60903f4.s: Which body, set up in 1953, dealt specifically with the formation of Andhra State?
naa8b60903f4.x: The sequence was Dhar (1948), JVP (1948-49), Wanchoo (1953, for Andhra) and Fazal Ali SRC (1953-55, all India).

nd63ba7cd5ee.s: Around 1910, Telugus formed about what share of the population of the Madras Presidency?
nd63ba7cd5ee.x: Telugus were about 40% (2 crore) of the Presidency, yet held only 8 high State jobs against 56 for non-Telugus.

n3f9c0099e8a.s: In 1954, the Andhra High Court was established at:
n3f9c0099e8a.x: The Andhra High Court was set up at Guntur in 1954; the Madras High Court retained jurisdiction until then.

n5ad412568ed.s: The Wanchoo Committee submitted its report on:
n5ad412568ed.x: Appointed on 7 February 1953, it reported on 23 March 1953; Nehru announced the capital on 25 March 1953.

n8a966332471.s: The Partition Committee (1949–50) on administrative arrangements for a new Andhra State was chaired by:
n8a966332471.x: The 1949–50 Partition Committee was chaired by Kumaraswamy Raja.

ne7dd4cf1aab.s: After Bellary was divided, the Tungabhadra Board for the works shared by Andhra and Mysore was set up under the:
ne7dd4cf1aab.x: The Tungabhadra Board was established under the Andhra State Act, 1953 to manage the shared works.

n0fde3dcff40.s: The Wanchoo Committee (1953) was appointed to deal with:
o: Boundaries, finances, assets and administration of the new Andhra State
Reorganisation of all Indian states on linguistic lines
Determining the permanent capital of India
n0fde3dcff40.x: Its terms covered boundary division, financial settlement, asset distribution and administrative arrangements, not the capital of India.

n724d6288ee6.s: The Wanchoo Committee recommended that the Andhra Government function temporarily, for three to five years, from:
n724d6288ee6.x: As Andhra lacked capital infrastructure, Wanchoo recommended working from Madras city for three to five years.

nac3ebe04c10.s: In the 2014 bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, the allocation of employees was handled by the:
nac3ebe04c10.x: The Kamalanathan Committee dealt with employees, the Sheela Bhide Committee with Schedule IX institutions and the Section 6 committee with the capital.

n73cdeceb878.shape: one-liner (NOT not possible: original has no false statement)
n73cdeceb878.s: Vartamana Tarangini, the first Telugu paper started by a Muslim, was begun at Madras in 1842 by:
n73cdeceb878.x: Syed Rahamatullah began the weekly at Madras on 8 June 1842; after 1843 it passed to Puvvada Seshagiri Rao.

nfefaf0a7913.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao started the Telugu paper Swarajya in 1907 at:
nfefaf0a7913.x: Gadicherla's Swarajya began at Vijayawada in 1907; Prakasam's Swarajya was a separate English daily from Madras.

n7ee8d99896f.shape: statements (one-liner not possible: no single confirmed fact with plausible same-kind decoys)
n7ee8d99896f.s:
Consider the following statements about newspapers in the Andhra region:
1. Newspapers gave rise to reading rooms and libraries.
2. Newspapers had no role beyond reporting political events.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n7ee8d99896f.x: Newspapers gave rise to reading rooms and libraries, so their influence went beyond reporting political events.

n456840ff696.s: Tattvabodhini, which supported widow remarriage, was published at Madras in 1864 by the:
n456840ff696.x: Tattvabodhini was published by the Madras Veda Samaj in 1864 and supported widow remarriage.

nf959df1545b.s: The first political journal in Telugu (1885) was:
nf959df1545b.x: Andhra Prakasika (1885) was the first Telugu political journal; Satyadoota (1835) was the first Telugu newspaper.

n03f572dcedf.shape: one-liner (NOT not possible: original has no false statement)
n03f572dcedf.s: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao (1867-1947) was known by the title:
n03f572dcedf.x: Nageswara Rao was titled 'Desoddharaka'; he used his Amrutanjan wealth for public work in the spirit of trusteeship.

n1478567e826.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao founded the Edward Corporation Library (now the Victoria Reading Room) at:
n1478567e826.x: He founded it at Nandyal with Kaderbad Narasinga Rao, not at Kurnool.

n5976768a11c.s: Sreebagh, the Madras house where the Sreebagh Pact was signed in 1937, belonged to:
n5976768a11c.x: Sreebagh was Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's house; the Pact was signed there on 16 November 1937.

n43db382e509.s: The newspaper Zamin Ryot was edited by:
n43db382e509.x: Venkatarama Naidu edited Zamin Ryot; Mutnuri edited Krishna Patrika, Nageswara Rao Bharati, and Chilakamarti Desamata and Manorama.

n67dc9592c1d.s: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao sent his newspaper, books and Bharati free to any group of ____ youths that opened a village library.
n67dc9592c1d.x: Any group of ten youths opening a village library received his newspaper, books and Bharati free.

n9e8936a388b.s: Mutnuri Krishna Rao transformed which paper into a political weekly and a hub of freedom fighters?
n9e8936a388b.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao made Krishna Patrika a political weekly and a centre of political awakening.

na0f6bb35a5d.shape: one-liner (NOT not possible: original has no false statement)
na0f6bb35a5d.s: Delegates from the Nizam's State attended the first Andhra library conference held at:
na0f6bb35a5d.x: The Nizam's State sent delegates to the first library conference at Vijayawada; Hyderabad State libraries shared the same revival.

n48fda56801e.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the original)
n48fda56801e.s: The first library conference in Andhra, held at Vijayawada, was attended by how many delegates?
n48fda56801e.x: About 200 delegates representing 60 libraries attended, including from Bellary and the Nizam's State.

n939c2bb54b4.s: Under colonial restrictions, the Andhra library movement functioned as a legal centre of:
n939c2bb54b4.x: Libraries served as legal centres of political education and built the Telugu identity behind the statehood demand.

n8d42581e9e1.s: Who was the first president of the Andhra Desa Library Association?
n8d42581e9e1.x: Mocherla Ramachandra Rao was the first president; Ayyanki and Nalam Krishnarao were secretaries.

nap-history-1-22.s: Who was the first Telugu writer to win the Jnanpith Award?
nap-history-1-22.x: Viswanatha Satyanarayana won the first Telugu Jnanpith.

n10c75646190.s: The Madras Public Libraries Act, 1948, shaped by the Andhra library movement, funded libraries through a:
n10c75646190.x: The Act created local library authorities and funded them through a library cess.

nd20e07863b5.s: Grandhalaya Sarvasvam, the first Telugu journal on library science, began in:
nd20e07863b5.x: It began in 1915 (some sources say 1916); 1913 was the year of the first library conference.

nap-history-11-4.x: Rajasekhara Charitram was the first Telugu novel.

nap-history-19-13.s: The Andhra Pradesh Sahitya Academy was established by the State Government in:
nap-history-19-13.x: The AP Sahitya Academy was set up in 1957 for Telugu literature, manuscripts and lexicons.

nap-history-11-17.s: The first Telugu library, Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam (Hyderabad, 1901), was founded by:
nap-history-11-17.x: Komarraju Lakshmana Rao founded it in 1901 to develop Telugu language and literature in Telangana.

nap-history-1-5.s: The first book printed in Telugu was:
nap-history-1-5.x: The Bible was the first book printed in Telugu.

n0d23853c8a9.s: The Gautami Granthalayam (1898) is located at:
n0d23853c8a9.x: Gautami Granthalayam is at Rajahmundry (1898); C.V.N. Granthalayam is at Ongole and Sujananda Granthalayam at Rayakuduru.

n6e50393630c.s: Who ran the boat library at Sangam Jagarlamudi?
n6e50393630c.x: Kotha Sivaramakrishnayya ran it; Pathuri Nagabhushanam ran the Bank Canal boat library.

nap-history-1-27.s: The first widow remarriage in Andhra, conducted by Veeresalingam on 11 December 1881, took place at:
nap-history-1-27.x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam conducted the first widow remarriage in Andhra at Rajahmundry on 11 December 1881.

nap-history-19-23.s: Komarraju Venkata Lakshmana Rao and his associates founded the Vignana Chandrika Mandali in:
nap-history-19-23.x: They founded the Bhasha Nilayam in 1901 and the Vignana Chandrika Mandali in 1906.

nap-history-19-10.s: The Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam, the first non-government Telugu library in Hyderabad, was founded in:
nap-history-19-10.x: It was founded in 1901; 1906 is the year of the Vignana Chandrika Mandali.

n4ee5baf02b2.s: Who is known as the 'Library Gandhi'?
n4ee5baf02b2.x: Velaga Venkatappayya is the 'Library Gandhi'; Paturi Nagabhushanam is 'Granthalayodyama Roopasilpi'.

nc06103ca2b6.s: One objection to the immediate merger of Telangana with Andhra was that it might affect Telangana's local-employment safeguards known as the:
nc06103ca2b6.x: The Telangana case feared that the Mulki rules and local jobs might be affected, along with diversion of its revenue surplus.

n192991f52c3.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 provided for a Telangana:
n192991f52c3.x: It provided a Telangana Regional Council, spending of surplus revenue in Telangana and retention of the Mulki rules.

n9ae7ec0f4c1.s: The Belgaum border dispute, which continued after linguistic reorganisation, is between:
n9ae7ec0f4c1.x: Border disputes such as Belgaum between Maharashtra and Karnataka continued after reorganisation.

n0104e36b2e8.s: Under the SRC's review mechanism (para 386), unification of Telangana with Andhra after 1961 required the support of ____ of the elected members of the Telangana Assembly.
n0104e36b2e8.x: The SRC required two-thirds of the elected members, not three-fourths.

nb9334336433.s: The States Reorganisation Commission regarded language as:
o: An important factor but not the only factor
The sole basis for forming states
A factor only for southern states
nb9334336433.x: The SRC treated language as important but not the only factor, rejecting 'one language, one state' and weighing national unity.

n85337d35962.s: The Seventh Constitutional Amendment (1956) abolished the office of:
n85337d35962.x: It abolished the office of Rajpramukh and replaced the Part A/B/C/D classification with states and Union Territories.

n1b08660082c.s: Which was the first state formed under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
n1b08660082c.x: Andhra Pradesh was the first state formed under the SR Act, 1956, not Mysore.

n318b505f984.s: The States Reorganisation Commission report (1955) recommended the creation of:
n318b505f984.x: The 1955 report proposed 16 states and 3 Union Territories and abolition of the Part A, B and C classification.

n025f5a43cd7.s: For Telangana, the States Reorganisation Commission had originally recommended:
n025f5a43cd7.x: The SRC initially recommended keeping Telangana separate; the 1956 merger followed the Gentlemen's Agreement.

n68140702fcb.s: Andhra State, the first state formed on a linguistic basis after independence, was carved out of:
n68140702fcb.x: Andhra State was formed from Madras State, with Kurnool (not Hyderabad) as capital.

n6eaf14728c8.s: Which of the following was an argument in favour of linguistic states?
o: It would impose one language for all administration
It would let people be governed in their own language
n6eaf14728c8.x: Governance in the people's language, preservation of cultural identity and easier administration were the arguments for linguistic states.

nd1fd9df75f2.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State (1953)?
nd1fd9df75f2.x: Tanguturi Prakasam was the first CM of Andhra State; N. Sanjiva Reddy was the first CM of Andhra Pradesh (1956).

nef0a29bdea8.s: The States Reorganisation Commission was formally constituted by a Home Ministry Resolution on:
nef0a29bdea8.x: Announced on 22 December 1953, it was formally constituted on 29 December 1953 and reported in 1955.

nfb289eb1698.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement was concluded on:
nfb289eb1698.x: The Agreement came on 20 February 1956, after the CMs agreed to merge (22 October 1955) and before AP's formation (1 November 1956).

nap-history-40-19.s: The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission was established in:
nap-history-40-19.x: The APPSC came in 1956, after the Dhar Commission (1948) and the SRC (1953).

nap-history-40-17.s: In which year was the States Reorganisation Commission set up?
nap-history-40-17.x: The SRC was set up in December 1953; Kailashnath Wanchoo was not a member.

naaa104a95e5.s: Who was the chairman of the States Reorganisation Commission (1953)?
naaa104a95e5.x: Syed Fazl Ali (then Governor of Odisha) chaired it; H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar were members.

nbad7ad9018c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2026 developments on the capital of Andhra Pradesh?
o: The AP Assembly passed a resolution on 28 March 2026.
The resolution sought naming Amaravati in Section 5(2) of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
The Lok Sabha passed the amendment Bill in June 2026.
The amendment made Hyderabad the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh.
nbad7ad9018c.x: The 2026 amendment made Amaravati, not Hyderabad, the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh.

n214fb16c4ff.s: The working of the Telangana Regional Committee was to be reviewed after:
n214fb16c4ff.x: The Committee's working was to be reviewed after ten years; disputes with the State Government went to the Centre.

nea85fa7eb21.s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement, at least how many of the portfolios of Home, Finance, Revenue, Planning and Development, and Commerce and Industry were to go to Telangana?
nea85fa7eb21.x: At least two of these portfolios were to go to Telangana, and the CM and Deputy CM were to be from different regions.

n760f1311656.s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement, Telangana's revenue surplus was to be:
o: Used to build the new capital
n760f1311656.x: The promise was that Telangana's surplus would be spent only on Telangana.

n41ac641ce87.s: Who was the first non-Congress Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
n41ac641ce87.x: N.T. Rama Rao was the first non-Congress CM; Congress ruled uninterrupted from 1956 until 1983.

n36f70ca0772.s: The APCC meeting at Kurnool on 30 September 1953 demanded Visalandhra with ____ as its capital.
n36f70ca0772.x: The 1953 Kurnool meeting, associated with Neelam Sanjiva Reddy, demanded Visalandhra with Hyderabad as capital.

n9500358d36f.s: Which Article of the Constitution reflects the legacy of the Gentlemen's Agreement's domicile-related protection?
n9500358d36f.x: Article 371D and local-cadre arrangements reflect the Agreement's domicile protection.

n37a376b2930.s: In the 1954 Visalandhra discussions, who warned that a separate Telangana would be weak and vulnerable to suppression of democratic forces?
n37a376b2930.x: Swami Ramananda Tirtha strongly supported Visalandhra and gave this warning.

n956998e5006.s: Who wrote 'The Emergence of Andhra Pradesh'?
n956998e5006.x: K.V. Narayana Rao wrote the book; Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao contributed pamphlets for Visalandhra.

na01b727544b.s: In August 1984, N.T. Rama Rao's government was dismissed by Governor:
na01b727544b.x: Governor Ram Lal dismissed NTR while he was in the US; Nadendla Bhaskara Rao was sworn in and resigned on 16 September 1984.

n80ca4f5caac.s: Before the formation of Andhra Pradesh, the Andhra Legislature met at ____ and unanimously resolved in favour of the merger.
n80ca4f5caac.x: The Andhra Legislature unanimously backed the merger at Kurnool, and both ministries resigned.

nc0616a27461.s: Who, along with Jonnavittula Gurunatham, sketched the idea of a united Andhra in 1912?
nc0616a27461.x: Unnava Lakshminarayana and Jonnavittula Gurunatham sketched it in 1912; Nyapati Subbarao proposed one rule for all Telugu areas in 1914.

na1c44a23697.s: In 1956, Andhra Pradesh was formed by merging the 11 districts of Andhra State with how many Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State?
na1c44a23697.x: The 11 Andhra districts merged with nine Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State; Kannada and Marathi areas went to Mysore and Bombay.

n6f040834442.s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956), Urdu was to be kept in Telangana's administration and courts for:
n6f040834442.x: Urdu was retained for five years (then reviewed by the Regional Council), not ten.

n8736ee93a68.s: The Hyderabad State Communist Party practically functioned as a branch of the Andhra Communist Party headquartered at:
n8736ee93a68.x: It worked as a branch of the Andhra party at Vijayawada; the Communists propagated Visalandhra.

n6f2cd5a79a1.s: The later dilution of the safeguards given at the formation of Andhra Pradesh contributed to the agitation of:
n6f2cd5a79a1.x: The safeguards were political assurances without constitutional enforcement, and their dilution fed the 1969 agitation.

nadb8c540c1b.s: Damodaram Sanjivayya, the second Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, took office on:
nadb8c540c1b.x: Sanjivayya became CM on 11 January 1960 and later became President of the Indian National Congress.

n48ce1da010e.s: When N.T. Rama Rao founded the Telugu Desam Party in 1982, the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh was:
n48ce1da010e.x: Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy was CM when the TDP was founded on 29 March 1982 (APPSC G2 2019).

n38e41c9e436.s: The Andhra-Madras boundary settlement that gave Tiruttani to Tamil Nadu was made by the:
n38e41c9e436.x: The Pataskar Award settled the boundary; the Wanchoo Committee (7 Feb 1953) was headed by K.N. Wanchoo, CJ of Rajasthan HC.

nd317e531b97.s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement, the financial arrangement for Telangana was to be reviewed after:
nd317e531b97.x: Common costs were shared proportionately, Telangana's surplus was to be spent in Telangana, and the arrangement reviewed after five years.

nf74b3c5d598.s: The Mulki agitation of 1952 took place under the ministry of:
nf74b3c5d598.x: It occurred under the Burgula ministry; police firing near City College, Hyderabad, killed students.

n6f0247a6cbd.s: Article 371D was inserted by the ____ Constitutional Amendment (1973) to implement the Six-Point Formula.
n6f0247a6cbd.x: The 32nd Amendment (1973) inserted Article 371D, providing equitable opportunities, local cadres and the AP Administrative Tribunal.

n1130f113b9d.s: Before the 1956 merger, Telangana's employment apprehension was that the ____ might be weakened.
n1130f113b9d.x: The employment concern was weakening of the Mulki Rules; other fears concerned the revenue surplus and regional disparities.

nf814cc80287.s: Who started the Visalandhra paper and became the first General Secretary of the CPI(M) in 1964?
nf814cc80287.x: P. Sundarayya started the Visalandhra paper and became the CPI(M)'s first General Secretary in 1964.

nb86151f51b7.s: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao founded the Visalandhra Mahasabha at Vijayawada in:
nb86151f51b7.x: He founded it on 26 November 1949 and raised the demand at the 1951 Bangalore Congress manifesto meeting.

n82235425a55.s: The Mulki rules of Hyderabad State originated in:
n82235425a55.x: The Mulki rules date from 1888 and were tightened by the Nizam's farman of 1919.

n5386a7603f1.s: The Warangal Congress meeting connected with the merger discussions was held on:
n5386a7603f1.x: The Warangal meeting was on 8 July 1954; the CMs met at Hyderabad House on 22 October 1955 and the Agreement came on 20 February 1956.

n71f156492ca.s: P.V. Narasimha Rao first became Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in:
n71f156492ca.x: The order was Sanjivayya (1960), Kasu Brahmananda Reddy (1964), P.V. Narasimha Rao (1971), T. Anjaiah (1980).

n03bb9c4b863.s: Swami Ramananda Tirtha, Burgula Ramakrishna Rao, Mandumula Narsing Rao and Pandit Narendraji all supported the:
n03bb9c4b863.x: All four supported the Visalandhra movement.

n0fd6aff14f2.s: Who had the shortest tenure as Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh, about 31 days in 1984?
n0fd6aff14f2.x: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao served 31 days (16 Aug - 16 Sep 1984).

n802fd420128.x: Sundarayya's book was published in 1946, after the 1912 and 1914 proposals and the 1936 Swaraj Party manifesto.

nap-history-25-19.s: Who was the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh during the Jai Andhra Movement of 1972?
nap-history-25-19.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao was CM when the Supreme Court's Mulki verdict set off the Jai Andhra Movement.

n7fb413d4d8c.s: The separate High Court of Andhra Pradesh began functioning at Amaravati on:
n7fb413d4d8c.x: After the common High Court (2014-2018), AP's separate High Court began at Amaravati on 1 January 2019.

n3e3bfc62bfc.s: The Telangana Regional Committee under the Gentlemen's Agreement was given constitutional backing through:
o: Article 371(1) and the 1958 Regional Committee Order
A separate Schedule of the Constitution
n3e3bfc62bfc.x: Backing came from Article 371(1) (Seventh Amendment, 1956) and the AP Regional Committee Order, 1958.

n008be9c537d.s: At the time of the Gentlemen's Agreement, the Chief Minister of Hyderabad State was:
n008be9c537d.x: Burgula was CM of Hyderabad State, K.V. Ranga Reddy its Deputy CM, and Bezawada Gopala Reddy CM of Andhra State.

nae6a77159fa.s: The first Governor of Andhra Pradesh, formed in 1956, was:
nae6a77159fa.x: C.M. Trivedi was the first Governor and Neelam Sanjiva Reddy the first Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.

n932d0ba3a13.s: Which party started the Visalandhra movement, won many seats in both regions in 1952 and expected a majority in a united state?
n932d0ba3a13.x: The Communist Party started the movement and expected a majority in a united Telugu state.

ndc33ba97b80.s: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy did not appoint a Deputy Chief Minister and described the post as a:
ndc33ba97b80.x: He called the post a 'sixth finger'; this breach fed the grievances behind the 1969 Jai Telangana movement.

n09019980d78.s: In 1968, the Telangana Regional Committee was extended for:
n09019980d78.x: It was extended for five years in 1968 and wound up after the 32nd Amendment (1973).

n8d216bec06c.s: The draft Bill for the state formed on 1 November 1956 proposed the name:
n8d216bec06c.x: The draft Bill used 'Andhra Telangana'; the Seventh Amendment Bill in the Lok Sabha settled on 'Andhra Pradesh'.

nf3ea434286f.s: In the 1983 election, the Telugu Desam Party won how many seats, forming the first non-Congress government in Andhra Pradesh?
nf3ea434286f.x: The TDP won 202 seats in 1983 and formed the first non-Congress government in AP.

n750f20f1b6e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Supreme Court judgment of October 1972?
o: It concerned the residence clause of the 1957 Public Employment Act.
It permitted non-locals to be barred from public posts in Hyderabad and Telangana.
It immediately contributed to the Jai Andhra Movement.
n750f20f1b6e.x: The 1972 ruling concerned the older Mulki Rules; the 1957 Act's residence clause had been struck down in 1969.

n815c85cc6ba.s:
Assertion (A): The GN Rao Committee and the BCG study formed the basis of the three-capitals plan of 2020.
Reason (R): The Sivaramakrishnan Expert Committee on the AP capital recommended a 'super capital'.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n815c85cc6ba.x: A is true. R is false: the Sivaramakrishnan Committee (report August 2014) opposed a 'super capital'.

n559844b63d3.s: The states created in 2000 were formed mainly on grounds of:
n559844b63d3.x: The 2000 states were created on grounds of tribal and regional backwardness, not language.

n4c966bcb142.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, liabilities and debt are apportioned according to:
n4c966bcb142.x: Liabilities and refunds go by population ratio, assets by location and tax arrears by place of assessment.

n16b32aa8b21.s: Which Section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 made Hyderabad the common capital?
n16b32aa8b21.x: Section 5 dealt with Hyderabad as common capital; Section 3 formed Telangana, Section 6 the capital expert committee and Section 8 the Governor's security role.

n115aa55adc2.s: Which Section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 extended Article 371D to Telangana?
n115aa55adc2.x: Section 97 extended Article 371D to Telangana; Section 10 added Telangana as Entry 29 in the First Schedule.

n67eaf55c123.s: A Bill under Article 3 can be introduced in Parliament only on the recommendation of the:
n67eaf55c123.x: It needs the President's recommendation; the State legislature's views are sought but not binding, and it passes by simple majority.

na4271f1bc6e.s: Which Part of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with the High Court?
na4271f1bc6e.x: Part IV deals with the High Court; Parts III, VI and VIII cover legislatures, assets and liabilities, and services.

na05e7eb4bb9.s: After the 2019 reorganisation, which Union Territory was provided no legislature?
na05e7eb4bb9.x: Ladakh has no legislature, while the UT of Jammu and Kashmir has a Legislative Assembly.

n3cc3afeb0c4.s: Under Article 371D, service disputes in Andhra Pradesh were placed under:
o: The exclusive jurisdiction of the High Court
n3cc3afeb0c4.x: Article 371D provided an Administrative Tribunal for service disputes, taking them out of the High Court's jurisdiction.

n6d1e396072c.s: Section 10 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 added Telangana as entry number ____ in the First Schedule.
n6d1e396072c.x: Section 10 added Telangana as entry 29; the Act was made under Articles 3 and 4, needing no Article 368 amendment.

n42346b37ee7.s: Under Article 16(3), residence requirements for public employment can be prescribed by:
n42346b37ee7.x: Article 16(3) empowers only Parliament; Article 371D is a special route for Andhra Pradesh.

n421618cf224.s: Under the 1975 zonal system of undivided Andhra Pradesh, Hyderabad was included in Zone:
n421618cf224.x: Hyderabad was in Zone VI; Zones I-III were Coastal Andhra, Zone IV Rayalaseema and Zones V-VI Telangana.

n5d9a77f68cb.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 made Amaravati the sole, permanent capital with effect from:
n5d9a77f68cb.x: It took effect from 2 June 2024, when Hyderabad's 10-year common-capital term ended, not 2 June 2014.

n0e143d4b29b.s: During the Jai Andhra Movement, protesters hoisted a separate Andhra State flag on:
n0e143d4b29b.x: The flag was hoisted on 10 December 1972, after the October 1972 Supreme Court judgment upholding the Mulki Rules.

nf582b28fd16.s: The one-man Girglani Commission examined violations of GO 610 and the:
nf582b28fd16.x: J.M. Girglani examined violations of GO 610 and the 1975 Presidential Order, finding many non-local appointments, especially in Zone VI.

ncb9be3d84f1.s: Provisions for IIT, NIT, IIM, AIIMS and a new railway zone for Andhra Pradesh are in which Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
ncb9be3d84f1.x: The Thirteenth Schedule lists these institutions, central and tribal universities and infrastructure such as a railway zone, steel plant, port and metros.

n7c502c0431d.s: The Central University at Hyderabad is associated with Article:
n7c502c0431d.x: The Central University is under Article 371E; Article 371D concerns local cadres and the AP Administrative Tribunal.

na6d59bed0f7.s: GO 610 (30 December 1985), to repatriate non-locals appointed in violation of the 1975 Presidential Order, was issued by the government of:
na6d59bed0f7.x: GO 610 was issued by the NTR (TDP) government; the Girglani Commission (2001) was set up by the Chandrababu Naidu government.

n27c1a3274fa.s: Under which Article can Parliament by law form a new State or alter the area, boundaries or name of a State?
n27c1a3274fa.x: Article 3 empowers Parliament to form new States and change their area, boundaries or names.

n830cb9c7631.s: The Telangana Rashtra Samithi was formed in:
n830cb9c7631.x: The TRS was formed in 2001, before the Centre's December 2009 announcement, the Srikrishna report (2010) and the Million March (2011).

n74bf503e2cf.s: Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Uttarakhand were formed in:
n74bf503e2cf.x: The three States were formed in 2000, between AP (1956) and Telangana (2014).

n37e90d2eb85.s: Under Section 5 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Hyderabad was to be the common capital for a period not exceeding:
n37e90d2eb85.x: Section 5 made Hyderabad the common capital for not more than ten years.

n3d212e1dea6.s: The 32nd Constitutional Amendment was enacted in:
n3d212e1dea6.x: The order was Jai Telangana (1969), Jai Andhra (1972), 32nd Amendment (1973), GO 610 (1985) and Girglani Report (2004).

n558b2d8bd76.s: Indira Gandhi announced the Eight-Point Formula on 11 April 1969 during the:
n558b2d8bd76.x: The Eight-Point Formula belongs to the Jai Telangana agitation; the Five-Point Formula of 27 November 1972 belongs to the Jai Andhra phase.

n2a3968b8e97.shape: one-liner (NOT not possible: original has no false statement)
n2a3968b8e97.x: The CPI(ML) was formed in 1969, viewed India as semi-feudal and followed the Chinese-model protracted guerrilla war.

nb43aab9454d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about N.G. Ranga and the peasant movement?
o: Ranga founded the Indian Peasants' Institute in 1933.
The Institute was located at Nidubrolu.
The All India Kisan Sabha was a mass organisation of the Congress.
Ranga was a founder of the All India Kisan Sabha in 1936.
nb43aab9454d.x: The AIKS was a mass organisation of the CPI, not the Congress.

n928cb54ea07.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Anti-arrack movement is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Broomsticks and chilli powder – used by women protesters
Legislative elections – main method of the movement
n928cb54ea07.x: Women closed shops and stopped auctions using broomsticks and chilli powder; legislative elections were not a method of the movement.

nf48c0558b15.s: Kusuma Dharmanna's Adi-Andhra Mahasabha of 1936 was held at:
nf48c0558b15.x: The 1936 Mahasabha was at Vizianagaram; Bhagya Reddy Varma's 1919 conference was at Machilipatnam.

n046608c63a2.s: Kaka Kalelkar is known for chairing the:
n046608c63a2.x: Kaka Kalelkar chaired the First National Backward Class Commission; he is not a figure of modern Dalit assertion in AP.
